A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Partial Gromov-Wasserstein research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original shape-matching, shape-retrieval, interpolation and solver-runtime experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds original multi-shape interpolation, parameter-sensitivity, expanded retrieval and positive-unlabeled classification results.

M1.justification: The PGW objective, general Frank-Wolfe solvers and barycenter algorithm are retained. Appendices P.1 and R add FLB-POT initialization and a PU-classification adaptation using prior-weighted masses and quantile thresholding. The PU implementation also replaces line-search step selection with a fixed step of 1.

E1.justification: v4 extends shape-focused evaluation to positive-unlabeled classification on MNIST, EMNIST and Caltech Office's Amazon, DSLR and Webcam domains with SURF/DECAF features. It also adds randomly rotated 4D retrieval scenarios and interpolation among four shapes in mixed ambient dimensions.

E2.justification: Comparisons expand beyond the previous GW-family emphasis. Appendix O.1 adds OT and UOT to the retained shape-retrieval datasets, while Appendix M.2 evaluates OT and partial-OT barycenters alongside GW and PGW. The original comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New PU protocols specify a known positive prior of 0.2, 4D/6D autoencoder embeddings, sample-size regimes and method-specific solver settings. Mixed-dimensional interpolation adds padding and PCA procedures. Appendix N also changes the reported UGW penalties from rho1=rho2=10 to 1; the unchanged Figure 1 does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Where v3 reports fixed shape-matching settings, v4 adds parameter sweeps for PGW, MPGW and UGW in Figure 10. It also compares PU initialization methods, visualizes embedding separability, and examines rotation and outlier sensitivity in the new multi-shape experiments.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly states that PU experiments were tested five times and averaged. It supplies no dispersion estimates, confidence intervals or seeds. The existing 10,000 nearest-neighbor repetitions and ten-fold cross-validation reporting are retained; no increase in runs for those experiments is established.

E6.justification: Table 1's original accuracies and runtimes are unchanged. v4 adds OT/UOT retrieval scores, parameter-sweep and multi-shape findings, and extensive PU accuracy/runtime results. Some new entries remain ambiguous: Tables 3 and 4 report 65% and 95%, respectively, for apparently corresponding UGW MNIST-to-EMNIST results with FLB-U initialization.

T1.justification: The principal existence, metric, solver-equivalence, convergence and barycenter proofs are retained. v4 adds formal PU assumptions, initialization objectives and a classification rule. Appendix L also restricts the counterexample's stated rho range from [0,100] in v3 Remark L.4 to (0,100] in v4 Remark L.5.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and summary retain the same central contributions: a PGW metric for general mm-spaces, equivalent Frank-Wolfe solvers, barycenters and effectiveness on shape tasks. The added appendix experiments do not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations involving OT's coordinate sensitivity, PU embedding separability and class-prior information, plus outlier-dependent guidance for choosing lambda. Existing local-minimum and MDS-orientation limitations are retained. The new blanket claim that OT/UOT underperform GW and all its variants overstates Table 2, particularly its MPGW results.

D1.justification: v4 adds an explicit PGW code-repository link, new dataset-access links, initialization and parameter-selection guidance, and PU implementation details covering embeddings, sample sizes, tolerances, iteration limits and numerical precision. Hardware information is retained. The PDFs establish these disclosures, not the external resources' functionality.

R1.justification: v4 adds references supporting PU learning, OT barycenters, domain datasets/features and unbalanced transport, including Bekker and Davis, Elkan and Noto, and Cuturi and Doucet. It relates FLB-POT to earlier initialization approaches. The introductory novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include copyediting, updated title hyphenation and affiliations, rearranged Appendix L examples, new appendix subsections, acknowledgments and removal of the generic impact statement. The scientific additions do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 adds multi-shape panels, parameter-sweep and embedding visualizations, and Tables 2–7, alongside changed page geometry and extensive figure placement changes. Some existing graphics are additionally duplicated: Figures 8/12 show the pairwise matrices and Figures 9/11 show the shape examples. The original runtime plot is retained as Figure 14.

improvement.justification: v4 improves practical assessment through parameter and initialization analyses, broader comparisons and applications, and better code-access and implementation information. The core theory and original results were already present in v3. Unexplained differences between PU Tables 3 and 4 and Appendix O.1's overgeneralization of Table 2 weaken the added evidence, limiting the net gain despite the useful expansion.
